text:
morgan: Anyone see weird 'resume_count' spikes around 08:15 UTC? panels show a 10x blip but traces for the same session show only one reconnect. :confused:
ash: Which panel/query? I can take a look.
morgan: Streaming -> Session Health -> resume_count (1m). query is `sum(increase(stream.resume_events[1m])) by (shard,env)` and the alert threshold fired. raw trace for session 9a2b: `resume=1` at 08:15:02.
telemetry-bot: alert: `resume_count > 500` (1m) at 2026-03-18T08:16:00Z. :rotating_light:
sre: Could be aggregation windowing causing duplicate attribution when proxy flips collector during scrape windows. We saw similar with heartbeat earlier but this looks time-bucket misalignment.
ash: I pulled metrics from two collectors for the same minute: collector-x emitted `increase(...[1m]) = 1` and collector-y emitted `=1` because the event straddled the scrape boundary and both collectors incremented their local counters. Since the dashboard sums by shard only, sum() collapses them into 2 for that minute.
morgan: ah, so two independent counters each saw the event once. When Prom scrapes both and we sum, we double-count unless we tag by `collector_id`.
lia: But we don't want dashboards with collector_id grouping — that would explode series. Short-term we can use `max` instead of `sum` for this metric across collectors if we're looking for per-shard peaks. e.g. `max by (shard,env) (increase(stream.resume_events[1m]))`
grafana-admin: Using `max` hides real multi-event bursts though. We need a robust fix in telemetry pipeline.
sre: Agreed. Two options: 1) ensure only a single collector emits a counter for a given session by preserving a stable `owner_id` tag, or 2) switch to using monotonic global counters at ingress and propagate them (harder).
telemetry-bot: note: rolling back alert to a higher threshold for 30m as a mitigation.
ash: Implementation detail: collector currently stores counters in process memory and increments on event. On handoff we flush and the new collector also counts when it observes the stream resume until it learns state. Race window is ~500ms and overlaps with Prom scrape intervals. We can attach `session_owner` tag when the first collector claims the session and keep that tag on subsequent metrics as `session_owner=<uuid>` so `sum` remains safe.
morgan: That sounds cleaner than changing dashboards. Any perf/regressions?
sre: Adding a stable tag is fine but it increases cardinality by number of concurrent sessions; however, `session_owner` would only be set for counter metrics we aggregate by session (resume, heartbeat), and we can restrict retention/ingest rules to drop that tag after 24h.
lia: Another idea: emit an `event_id` with each resume and attach it as a tag. TSDB can dedupe if we use `topk`/unique constraints but most TSDBs don't dedupe on tag value. Not reliable.
grafana-admin: For now I'll change the panel to `max by (shard,env) (increase(stream.resume_events[1m]))` and add a note to the panel description: "temporary mitigation: collector handoff causes double-counts; backend fix in progress."
ash: I'll open a tiny PR to add `session_owner` to resume/heartbeat counters and ensure the handoff process preserves it. Also adding idempotency_key on the emitter for retries so retry sends carry the same key.
sre: Also file an issue for the scrape alignment problem — maybe we can add a short jitter in collector flush to avoid both collectors incrementing within the same scrape window. But jitter alone is brittle.
morgan: Can we add a metric-level dedupe in the ingestion path keyed on `event_uuid`? That might be heavier but the most accurate.
sre: ingestion dedupe is expensive at scale, prefer fixing producer side.
lia: I'll coordinate with observability to lower alert noise; we don't want oncall chasing duplicates.
telemetry-bot: action: alert threshold bumped; annotation added: "investigating collector handoff double-counting".
grafana-admin: Patch rolled to dashboards. PRs: #5824 (panel change), #5825 (panel note).
ash: I'll start the emitter patch today and send a canary. assigning to myself.
sre: filing infra issue for collector ownership TTL and handoff preservation (#4187).
morgan: thanks all - this saved a noisy wake-up. :coffee:
